message.content: The last common ancestor of lions (Felidae) and zebras (Equidae) is the ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**—the group that includes carnivores, perissodactyls, artiodactyls, bats, and cetaceans. This ancestor lived roughly 90 million years ago and is an extinct lineage rather than a living species.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. This is a biology question. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). Both are mammals, specifically within the order Carnivora for lion and order Perissodactyla for zebra. But they share a more distant common ancestor at the level of class Mammalia. But maybe they want the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of lion and zebra. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Felidae (lion) and Equidae (zebra). That would be the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals? Actually lion is a placental mammal, as is zebra. So the MRCA is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Felidae and Equidae. That is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals? Wait, lion is a member of the family Felidae, which is part of the order Carnivora, which is part of the superorder Laurasiatheria. Zebra is a member of the family Equidae, which is part of the order Perissodactyla, also part of Laurasiatheria. So the MRCA of lion and zebra is the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That is the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. That would be the ancestor of the group that includes orders like Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla, Chiroptera, Cetartiodactyla, etc. So the answer: the common ancestor is the ancestor of Laurasiatheria. Or we can say the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both Felidae and Equidae is the ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. Alternatively, if we want a specific species, it's not known. It's an extinct ancestor. So we can say the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria, which lived around 90 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria.
